# Journal of Thoracic Disease

> > A peer-reviewed medical journal publishing cutting-edge research on thoracic diseases, cancer biology, and respiratory procedures with focus on molecular mechanisms and clinical innovations.

The Journal of Thoracic Disease is a comprehensive medical research platform covering cardiothoracic surgery, oncology, and pulmonary medicine. The journal publishes original research, clinical studies, and reviews advancing treatment and understanding of thoracic conditions.

## Key Topics

- esophageal cancer
- ferroptosis
- lncRNA (long non-coding RNA)
- KRAS mutations
- non-small cell lung cancer
- rigid bronchoscopy
- photodynamic therapy
- atrial fibrillation
- aortic dissection
- biomarkers
- clinical advancement
- transcriptomic profiling
- non-invasive ventilation
- cancer progression
- thoracic disease

## Cancer Biology & Molecular Mechanisms

- [Long non-coding RNA LINC00092 inhibits esophageal squamous cell carcinoma progression by promoting ferroptosis through the MAZ/NFE2L2 axis](https://jtd.amegroups.org/article/view/111744/rc): Research on LINC00092 lncRNA inhibiting esophageal cancer via ferroptosis and the MAZ/NFE2L2 signaling pathway
- [ATR expression as a prognostic biomarker in KRAS-mutated non-small cell lung cancer](https://jtd.amegroups.org/article/view/103535/coif): ATR biomarker prognostic study in KRAS-mutated non-small cell lung cancer with implications for treatment selection

## Clinical Treatment & Therapeutic Innovation

- [Photodynamic therapy as a promising treatment for long-segment and whole-circumferential early esophageal cancer](https://jtd.amegroups.org/article/view/99391/rc): Clinical research on photodynamic therapy efficacy for early esophageal cancer treatment
- [Innovation in rigid bronchoscopy—past, present, and future](https://jtd.amegroups.org/article/view/74654/pdf): Comprehensive review of rigid bronchoscopy innovations and clinical advancements in respiratory procedures
- [Non-invasive positive pressure ventilation can reduce perioperative mortality in acute aortic dissection patients with hypoxemia](https://jtd.amegroups.org/article/view/90710/dss): Clinical study demonstrating non-invasive ventilation effectiveness in reducing mortality in aortic dissection patients

## Cardiovascular & Transcriptomic Research

- [Integrated bulk sequencing and single-cell transcriptomic profiling implicates neutrophil-driven hypoxia in atrial fibrillation development](https://jtd.amegroups.org/article/view/107395/coif): Advanced transcriptomic study linking neutrophil-driven hypoxia mechanisms to atrial fibrillation pathogenesis
